title: Kähler differentials after completion
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], $\mathfrak p\subset S$ a maximal ideal, $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$, $F=S/\mathfrak p$, and $\widehat A=\varprojlim_rA/\mathfrak m^r$ the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Assume $F/k$ is finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], choose a $k$-algebra section $\sigma:F\to\widehat A$ of the residue map, and let $F$ act on $\widehat A$ and on each $\widehat A/\mathfrak m^r\widehat A=A/\mathfrak m^r$ through $\sigma$. Define the module of continuous $F$-differentials of $\widehat A$ as $\widehat\Omega_{\widehat A/F}=\varprojlim_r\Omega_{(\widehat A/\mathfrak m^r\widehat A)/F}$ (Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], transition maps induced by the quotient maps) with the derivation $\widehat{\mathrm d}_F:\widehat A\to\widehat\Omega_{\widehat A/F}$, $x\mapsto(\mathrm d(x\bmod\mathfrak m^r))_r$. Then: (i) the universal derivation $\mathrm d:A\to\Omega_{A/k}$ extends uniquely to a $k$-derivation $\widehat d:\widehat A\to\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] that is continuous for the $\mathfrak m$-adic topologies; (ii) there is a unique $\widehat A$-linear isomorphism $\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\widehat A\to\widehat\Omega_{\widehat A/F}$ sending $\mathrm d a\otimes1$ to $\widehat{\mathrm d}_F(a)$ for $a\in A$, and it carries $\widehat d(x)$ to $\widehat{\mathrm d}_F(x)$ for every $x\in\widehat A$.

proof.text: Every ideal of $k$ is $(0)$ or $(1)$, so $k$ is Noetherian. Finite-type Noetherianity and localization give Noetherian $S$ and $A$; thus $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated. Put $M=\Omega_{A/k}$. Leibniz expansion shows that differentials of algebra generators generate $\Omega_{S/k}$, and localization of differentials shows that $M$ is finite over $A$.

Put $N=\varprojlim_{r\ge1}M/\mathfrak m^rM$. Finite-module completion, after the tensor flip $m\otimes c\mapsto c\otimes m$, identifies $M\otimes_A\widehat A$ with $N$ by $m\otimes c\mapsto c\,j(m)$, where $j$ is the completion map. Completeness gives separated $N$, $Q_r=N/\mathfrak m^rN=M/\mathfrak m^rM$, and $B_r=\widehat A/\mathfrak m^r\widehat A=A/\mathfrak m^r$, all canonically, with surjective projections.

Apply [lem-trf-module-valued-derivation-completion] to $I=\mathfrak m$ and $d=\mathrm d$. This gives the unique continuous extension $D:\widehat A\to N$, the bound $D(\mathfrak m^{r+1}\widehat A)\subseteq\mathfrak m^rN$, and its lift formula at every $r\ge1$. This proves (i).

source.place: Tag 07PE (lemma-derivation-extends), proof of (1), module-valued form of the shifted quotient construction and uniqueness argument from the returned item, old Step 2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-adic-differential-quotient-interleaving] to this $D$ and the given finite separable $F/k$ and section. Reindex [def-trf-continuous-kahler-differentials] by $r=n+1$. With $E_r=\Omega_{B_r/F}$ obtain $D\sigma=0$ and $\alpha_r,\beta_r$ with their four identities. Define $\Phi(y)_r=\alpha_r(y_r)$ and $\Psi(z)_r=\beta_r(z_{r+1})$. The first transition identity makes $\Phi(y)$ compatible. For $\Psi$, $q_r\beta_{r+1}(z_{r+2})=\beta_rt_{r+1}(z_{r+2})=\beta_r(z_{r+1})$; completeness identifies this family with an element of $N$. Both maps are $\widehat A$-linear. The composite identities give $(\Psi\Phi y)_r=q_r(y_{r+1})=y_r$ and $(\Phi\Psi z)_r=t_r(z_{r+1})=z_r$ at every $r\ge1$, so they are inverse.

proof.text: For $x\in\widehat A$ lift it by $a\in A$ modulo $\mathfrak m^{r+1}\widehat A$. The lift formula and $\alpha_r$ give $(\Phi D(x))_r=\mathrm d(x\bmod\mathfrak m^r)$, hence $\Phi D=\widehat{\mathrm d}_F$. This includes the required images of $\mathrm da\otimes1$. Those tensors generate by the symbol presentation of $M$ and scalar extension; therefore their images determine any $\widehat A$-linear map uniquely, proving (ii).
